title: How far does a motorbike go in three hours at the same speed?
description: Harpreet's uncle rides a motorbike on the highway. The video builds the distance hour by hour and then multiplies to check it.
teaching_notes: One idea: distance in many hours is the distance in one hour taken again for each hour. Watch for children who add the hours to the kilometres.

source: A motorbike covers 50 km in one hour. How far does it go in
video_script.why: The child knows the distance in one hour but has not yet found it for many hours at the same speed.
video_script.substitution: Build the distance hour by hour, then multiply the distance in one hour by the number of hours.
video_script.anchor: Harpreet's uncle on a motorbike on the highway near Ludhiana
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu adds the three hours to the fifty kilometres. Hours and kilometres are different things, and each hour adds fifty more kilometres.
video_script.payoff_line: the bike goes one hundred and fifty kilometres in three hours
maths_rules: speed: 50 km in 1 hour; same speed all the time
1 hour: 50 km; 2 hours: 50 + 50 = 100 km; 3 hours: 100 + 50 = 150 km
your turn: 70 km in 1 hour, 4 hours: 70 × 4 = 280 km; never shown
video_script.design: One idea: each hour adds the same distance. Wrong idea: add the hours to the kilometres. The road of blocks stays on the stage; Chintu's bubble clears for the idea.

narration: <bookmark mark='m53'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='m54'/>Harpreet's uncle rides a motorbike on the highway near Ludhiana.
<bookmark mark='m55'/>It covers fifty kilometres in one hour.
<bookmark mark='m56'/>How far does it go in three hours at the same speed?

marks.m60: the other blocks outline the same size
marks.m61: three blocks line up end to end

narration: <bookmark mark='m58'/>Picture the long road as a row of equal blocks.
<bookmark mark='m59'/>One hour is one block, and each block is fifty kilometres long.
<bookmark mark='m60'/>The speed stays the same, so every block has the same size.
<bookmark mark='m61'/>We need three such blocks, placed end to end along the road.

beats.on_screen: Chintu's bubble shows 50 + 3 = 53; the 3 is circled as hours and the 50 as kilometres; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

marks.m63: the 3 is circled as hours and the 50 as kilometres
marks.m64: the bubble is struck through in the warning colour
marks.m65: an arrow shows 50 more km for each block

narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='m62'/>Fifty kilometres and three hours make fifty three kilometres.
<bookmark mark='m63'/>Three counts the hours, and fifty counts the kilometres.
<bookmark mark='m64'/>We cannot add hours to kilometres, since they measure different things.
<bookmark mark='m65'/>Each hour brings fifty more kilometres.

beats.on_screen: the blocks fill in with running totals: 50 km, 100 km, 150 km; the last total glows

marks.m68: the third block fills with 100 + 50 = 150 km

narration: <bookmark mark='m66'/>After one hour, the bike has gone fifty kilometres.
<bookmark mark='m67'/>After two hours, we add fifty again to get one hundred.
<bookmark mark='m68'/>After three hours, we add fifty once more to get one hundred and fifty.
<bookmark mark='m69'/>The bike goes one hundred and fifty kilometres in three hours.

beats.on_screen: the three blocks of 50 become one line: 50 × 3 = 150 km; 5 tens × 3 = 15 tens

marks.m70: the three blocks fold into one line
marks.m73: the line = 150 km appears and matches the total

narration: <bookmark mark='m70'/>There is a quicker way to find the same total.
<bookmark mark='m71'/>Three blocks of fifty means fifty multiplied by three.
<bookmark mark='m72'/>Five tens, three times, make fifteen tens.
<bookmark mark='m73'/>Fifteen tens are one hundred and fifty, the same as before.

beats.on_screen: the stage clears; the line distance in many hours is the distance in one hour multiplied by the number of hours; then a new line: a bus goes 70 km in 1 hour, 4 hours, and an empty box

marks.m75: the bus line appears with an empty box

narration: <bookmark mark='m74'/>The distance in many hours is the distance in one hour multiplied by the number of hours.
